answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a bond in a scarce, slashable token before it may claim tasks. When an agent submits fabricated work, an audited challenge can prove the failure and burn part of its bond, while successful work earns fees that gradually repay the stake. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence for free: every account needs locked capital, and each risky claim exposes that capital to loss. Even yarrow, dawn, and umber must each carry their own bond.
